city.notes: Join is exact-string address match between the DogCity foundation lot registry and the Runestone holder snapshot at block 962795. RECONCILIATION: all 112,384 stones and all 62,997 stone-holding addresses are accounted for; 49,446 stones (44.00%) sit on 29,138 city lots, and the remaining 62,938 stones are held by 33,859 addresses that own no lot. Those two buckets sum to 112,384 and 62,997 exactly, so nothing is lost or double counted. Every district, typology, height_tier and state breakdown sums back to 84,639 lots / 29,138 lots_with_stones / 49,446 stones. ONE LOT PER ADDRESS: lots.json holds 84,639 lots across 84,639 distinct addresses (zero duplicates), so a lot count and a stone-holding-address count are the same number by construction; stone_addresses_in_city (29,138) therefore equals totals.lots_with_stones. WHY 33,859 HOLDERS ARE OUTSIDE THE CITY: a lot exists only for a DOG holder above dust in the 2026-07-10 foundation snapshot (86,252 holders, 1,613 dust-dropped, 84,639 eligible per report.json). A Runestone holder who holds no DOG, holds under the dust floor, or first acquired DOG after 2026-07-10 has no lot and cannot appear here. This is not a data gap in the stone side; the stone side is complete. STALENESS: the two Runestone inputs are current and mutually consistent (runestone_holders_today.json and last_move.json both report tip 962795; inscriptions.jsonl has all 112,384 lines with 0 stale flags and 0 missing addresses, and its per-address counts are byte-identical to the holders file). The lot registry is the frozen foundation snapshot generated 2026-07-10T21:02:14.829Z, 37 days older than the stone snapshot generated 2026-08-16T23:27:44+00:00, and it is labelled stale in the staleness block so the page can say so. GENESIS CORE: district 0 and the ring0_visionary flag are the same 85 lots exactly (all 85 ring0 lots are in district 0 and all 85 district-0 lots are ring0), so the district row and the genesis_core block are two views of one cohort, not additive. report.json flags ring0_visionary as a PROVISIONAL proxy (the 85 earliest position_score wallets), not the final Satoshi Visionary cohort, so the page should not present it as settled. DEFINITIONS: share_pct is lots_with_stones / lots * 100 for that group; stones_share_of_city_pct is that district's stones as a share of the 49,446 in-city stones, not of all 112,384. EDGE CASE: height_tier 9 holds 7 lots and none of them belongs to a stone holder, so its share_pct is a true 0.0, not a missing value. Case-insensitive matching was tested and adds 0 further matches, and no address on either side carries stray whitespace. FULL DETAIL ON DISK: the complete 81-row Genesis Core roster with per-address stone counts is at genesis_core.holders in this file, alongside height_tiers and states breakdowns that are not part of the summary contract.

cohort_timeseries.notes: COHORT DEFINITION. The split is a fixed, present-day classification applied backwards to every daily snapshot. An airdrop wallet is a KEEPER if runestone_holders_today.json (tip 962795, generated 2026-08-16T23:27:44+00:00) shows it holding >= 1 Runestone right now, and a SELLER if it shows 0. Membership never changes across the series, so a rising keepers_dog line means today's stone-keeping wallets were already accumulating DOG, not that wallets switched groups. Result: 44,690 of the 75,497 airdrop wallets still hold a stone, 30,807 hold none. RECONCILIATION. inscriptions.jsonl carries 112,384 stone lines across 62,997 distinct addresses, matching runestone_holders_today.json exactly on both counts (112,384 stones, 62,997 addresses), and no line is flagged stale. Those 62,997 stone addresses split into 44,690 that are also airdrop wallets (holding 70,628 stones) and 18,307 that are not (holding 41,756 stones); 44,690 + 18,307 = 62,997 and 70,628 + 41,756 = 112,384. The 18,307 non-airdrop stone addresses are outside this time series by construction: the series only covers the 75,497 airdrop wallets the forensic snapshots track. Address matching is exact-string; a case-insensitive recheck found 0 additional matches, so no wallet is misfiled as a seller through address casing. GAPS. The 112,384 stones sit on 111,860 distinct outputs (147 outputs carry more than one stone). last_move.json resolves a height for 111,858 of those outputs, so 2 outputs holding 1 stone each have no last-move height: 2c29aa2af4e89d00b0449a0ea5c7067db1b9ff216e1c95c136dd5f209e49f618:10 and 7714427e5a7f7b959b056abf6e81967d7a57a696ffce8c29fbff35cbeeca3da2:1. This affects nothing in the series, which keys on address rather than on move height, but it is why any stone-age view built from last_move.json will cover 112,382 of 112,384 stones. STALENESS. The stone index and the DOG index do not stand at the same block. runestone_holders_today.json and last_move.json both stand at tip 962795. The last daily snapshot, forensic_2026-08-16.json, was taken at 2026-08-16T07:24:42.221Z at block 962,690, which is 105 blocks and about 17 hours behind that tip. The standalone baseline forensic_behavioral_analysis.json is fresher than the last daily snapshot: 2026-08-16T23:27:34.647Z at block 962,799, four blocks AHEAD of the stone tip. It is reported separately under "anchor" rather than folded into the series, so the 109 series points stay one generator, one cadence. The anchor confirms the last series point closely: keeper share 94.564669 percent versus 94.561912 percent, keepers 28,838,481,158.48 DOG versus 28,839,461,847.82 DOG, a drift of about 980,689 DOG (0.0034 percent) over the 109 blocks between the two readings. COVERAGE. 109 daily points, 2026-04-30 through 2026-08-16, no gaps and no duplicate dates. Every filename date matches its internal timestamp date on all 109 files. Every file carries exactly 75,497 profiles with 75,497 distinct addresses, and statistics.current_block rises monotonically from 947,216 to 962,690, a span of 15,474 blocks over 108 elapsed days. METHOD AND PRECISION. Each 42 MB file was streamed from the byte offset of "all_profiles":[ with a chunked regex, never more than one 8 MB window in memory, and the extractor was validated against a full json.load of forensic_2026-08-16.json: 75,497 of 75,497 address and balance pairs identical, 0 mismatches. Balances carry at most 5 decimal places and were summed as exact Decimals; keepers_dog and sellers_dog are those exact sums cast to float for charting, and keepers_dog_exact and sellers_dog_exact keep the full decimal string so nothing is rounded away. keeper_share_pct is the exact ratio rounded to 6 decimals. "live" counts addresses with current_balance > 0. WHAT THE SERIES SAYS. Over the 108 days the keeper cohort's DOG rose 0.2483 percent (28.768B to 28.839B) while the seller cohort's fell 24.5467 percent (2.198B to 1.659B), pushing keeper share of the airdrop supply from 92.901726 to 94.561912 percent, a monotone-ish climb with no reversal larger than a few hundredths of a point. Live wallets fell in both groups (keepers 25,454 to 25,129, down 1.2768 percent; sellers 2,359 to 2,038, down 13.6075 percent), so the keeper line is holding value with fewer wallets while the seller line is bleeding both. Note that only 25,129 of the 44,690 keeper wallets and 2,038 of the 30,807 seller wallets still hold any DOG at all on the last day: most airdrop wallets in both groups are empty of DOG, and the stone split explains where the remaining DOG sits, not how many wallets survive. NO SOURCE FILE UNDER DogData-v1/data WAS MODIFIED; this run only read them.

diamond_lost.notes: Sources reconcile. inscriptions.jsonl (112,384 lines, 0 stale) aggregated by address is exactly equal to the stones map in runestone_holders_today.json: 62,997 addresses, 112,384 stones; both Runestone sources are at tip 962795. lost_addresses_relaxed.csv is a strict subset of diamond_paws.csv (5,920 of 19,454), and the never-spent set recomputed from chain_stats.jsonl (chain_spent_txo_count == 0) is the same 5,920 addresses exactly, so the 'lost' and 'provably dormant' figures are one and the same set. DIAMOND PAWS: 18,790 of 19,454 (96.59%) still hold at least one Runestone, together 22,954 stones = 20.42% of the whole 112,384 supply, and 19,333,704,768 DOG. The 664 that hold DOG but no stone still sit on 757,224,906 DOG. In reverse, 44,207 of the 62,997 stone-holding addresses are not diamond paws and hold 89,430 stones (79.58%). 1 Runestone = 889,806 DOG: every one of the 19,454 airdrop amounts is an exact integer multiple, so the cohort's implied snapshot holding was 22,579 stones against 22,954 today, net +375. Per wallet: 18,254 unchanged, 473 hold more than at the snapshot, 727 hold fewer. Largest single diamond-paw stack is 124 stones; 17,508 of the 18,790 hold exactly one. TX ACTIVITY (stone-holding diamond paws, n=18,790): median 24, p90 183, max 255,126, min 3. single_tx_wallets is 0 and there is no wallet with 2 either - the floor is 3 txs (2 wallets), 508 wallets have 5 or fewer. A wallet needed at least a Runestone receive plus the DOG airdrop receive, so a 1-tx lifetime is structurally impossible in this cohort. LOST / NEVER-SPENT: all 5,920 still hold a stone (none is stoneless), 6,472 stones = 5.76% of supply, 5,635,141,398 DOG (5.64% of the 100B supply); addr_types p2tr 5,540, p2wpkh/p2wsh 262, p2pkh 67, p2sh 51. Because every lost wallet holds a stone, lost.airdrop_dog equals the whole-cohort DOG total. Implied snapshot 6,333 stones vs 6,472 today, +139: stones were sent INTO wallets that have never spent, which the never-spent rule permits. Consistent with that, 6,428 of the 6,472 stones last moved in 2024 (median block 834,785, 2024-03-15) and 44 later (41 in 2025, 3 in 2026, latest block 952,952, 2026-06-09). OUTLIER WARNING: three well-known burn addresses sit inside the lost cohort, each with 1 stone and 889,806 DOG - 1111111111111111111114oLvT2 (255,126 txs), 1BitcoinEaterAddressDontSendf59kuE (5,521), 1CounterpartyXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXUWLpVr (3,122). They never spend by construction, so they pass the never-spent filter and they alone set tx_count_max. Excluding all three, max is 63,559 for diamond paws and 1,753 for the lost cohort; medians and p90 are unchanged. HARD PROVABLY DORMANT: 6,472 stones held by 5,920 wallets that have never spent a single output. DOES NOT RECONCILE / CAVEATS: (1) 2 of the 112,384 stone outputs have no entry in last_move.output_height, so any last-move statistic over the full set covers 112,382; all 6,472 lost-cohort stones did resolve, so the dates above are complete. (2) last_move.json holds 111,858 outputs for 112,384 stones because stones share outputs when bundled - that is expected, not a gap. (3) The cohort CSVs carry no tip; their producer re-ran at 23:32:37Z during this analysis, 5 minutes after the 23:27:44Z holder snapshot, and rebuilt the identical cohorts (stale_removed 0, lost_newly_active 0), so a few blocks of drift are possible but nothing measurable shows up. All figures come from the post-rerun files. (4) 'kept_dog_sold_stone' means the wallet holds its full DOG airdrop and holds no stone today; the airdrop proves it held a stone at the snapshot, but the data here cannot say whether the stone was sold, gifted or moved to another wallet.

price_moves.notes: Every figure is computed from the inputs named below, no estimates. Universe: 112384 Runestone inscriptions (inscriptions.jsonl), of which 112382 resolve to a last-move block through last_move.json output_height (tip 962795). 2 stones do not: their current outputs (2c29aa2af4e89d00b0449a0ea5c7067db1b9ff216e1c95c136dd5f209e49f618:10, 7714427e5a7f7b959b056abf6e81967d7a57a696ffce8c29fbff35cbeeca3da2:1) are absent from output_height, so they are excluded from every count here; 112382 + 2 = 112384, reconciled. A stone's last-move date is the UTC date of the block that produced its current output (height -> unix time via height_time). Move dates run 2024-03-14 to 2026-08-16. Address reconciliation: inscriptions.jsonl carries 62997 distinct addresses summing to 112384 stones, and runestone_holders_today.json carries 62997 addresses summing to 112384 stones at the same tip (962795); the 62,997 / 112,384 totals match exactly. MONTHLY: stones_moved is the count of stones whose last move falls in that calendar month; avg_price is the unweighted mean of dog_price_history daily closes inside the month and avg_mvrv the unweighted mean of surviving_cohort_history mvrv_ratio inside the month, both null where the series does not cover the month. The price/MVRV series start 2024-04-24, so 2024-03 is null on both and 2024-04 averages only the 7 days 2024-04-24..2024-04-30 - the two distribution months are therefore not comparable to later months on price. 2026-08 is a partial month: stones through 2026-08-16, price through 2026-08-15 (15 days), MVRV through 2026-08-16 (16 days); see monthly_coverage for the day counts behind every average. PRICE BANDS: deciles of the per-stone price distribution over the 55928 stones whose last-move date has a DOG price; the other 56454 moved before the price series begins (2024-03-14..2024-04-23, the airdrop distribution window) and are excluded from the histogram, which is why the bands sum to 55928, not 112384. Bands are half-open [from, to) with the top band closed at the maximum observed price (0.009541); counts are uneven because tens of thousands of stones share a single day's price, so a decile boundary cannot split a day. Observed price range on move days: 0.000478 to 0.009541. VS REALIZED: 55928 stones have a last-move date with a surviving_cohort_history row; 34342 moved on a day when DOG price sat above realized price (61.4%), 21586 below, 0 exactly at it. The remaining 56454 stones moved before 2024-04-24 and have no cohort row. Read it as market-wide profit/loss context on the move day, not the mover's own cost basis - the inputs carry no per-stone acquisition price. Sources: dog_price_history.json and surviving_cohort_history.json agree to the last digit on all 844 shared days, so the cohort price was used as the price for 2026-08-16 (present in the cohort file, not yet in the price file). STALENESS: last_move.json and runestone_holders_today.json are both at tip 962795 (block time 2026-08-16T22:01:05+00:00); dog_price_history ends 2026-08-15, one day behind the tip day 2026-08-16, and surviving_cohort_history ends 2026-08-16, level with the tip day. No inscription carries stale=true. Label the newest bar as incomplete on the page.

two_clocks.notes: SCOPE. 112,384 stones across 62,997 addresses were read from inscriptions.jsonl and reconcile EXACTLY with runestone_holders_today.json (same 62,997 addresses, same per-address counts, zero mismatches, zero addresses present in only one file). No inscription row carried stale=true. STONE CLOCK. A stone dormancy is the time since the block that produced its current output (output_height in last_move.json); a wallet's oldest stone is the one with the LOWEST height, i.e. the LARGEST days value. 2 of 112,384 stones (0.00178%) have an output absent from output_height, so no height and no dormancy: 4727db8e...i289 (bc1qwelntg7tpxwgmh7gea0kycclx87mksnvhaadgf) and 14ed75c0...i289 (16MrRM5s4kGUBgK9CJbJGiH5dLQMMs84kU). Each of those addresses holds exactly 1 stone and holds NO DOG, so they drop out of the all-holders stone marginals (62,995 addresses / 112,382 stones instead of 62,997 / 112,384) and affect neither the matrix nor the correlation. That is the ONLY place totals do not reconcile to the headline numbers, and that is why. SHARED EPOCH. Both clocks are measured against one instant: holders_by_age.meta.generated_at = 2026-08-16T23:26:28Z (unix 1786922788). last_move.json height_time only carries the 26,783 heights that actually appear in output_height, so the tip block (962,795) has no timestamp there; the newest timestamped block is 962,787 at 2026-08-16T22:01:05Z, 85.38 minutes before the reference instant. That 0.059-day offset is far below any band boundary and moves no wallet between cells. STALENESS. Nothing is stale in a way that changes the result: last_move.json and runestone_holders_today.json both report tip 962,795; runestone_holders_today.json was generated 2026-08-16T23:27:44Z and holders_by_age.json 2026-08-16T23:26:28Z, 76 seconds apart. inscriptions.jsonl is the oldest file on disk (mtime 2026-08-16T22:47:13Z, 39 min before holders_by_age.json and 40 min before the stone snapshot; last_move.json is 23:12:45Z), but it is used only for the stone-to-output mapping and its address/count aggregation matches the 23:27:44Z snapshot exactly, so it is not behind in any observable way. BASELINE VS RUNESTONE. Baseline lth_pct 74.2698% is meta.lth_pct over all 85,895 DOG holders (supply-weighted, lth_dog/total_dog). The Runestone figure 93.8103% is computed the same way (sum lth_dog / sum total_dog) but only over the 29,198 addresses that hold both stones and DOG. Delta +19.5405 points. OVERLAP. 29,198 of 62,997 Runestone addresses (46.3482%) also hold DOG; they hold 49,658 stones (44.186% of all stones) and 35,589,388,638.95 DOG (35.5981% of the 99,975,593,202.33 DOG in the snapshot). The other 33,799 Runestone addresses hold 62,726 stones and no DOG at all, so they appear only in the stone marginals. LTH-DOMINANT. 28,647 of 29,198 (98.1129%) have lth_pct > 50 as asked; using >= 50 instead gives 28,663, so 16 wallets sit exactly at 50.0. COIN AGE AVERAGES. Address-weighted 755.3061 d, stone-weighted 667.2288 d, DOG-weighted 702.8546 d. The stone-weighted figure is LOWER than the address-weighted one, meaning wallets holding many stones tend to hold younger DOG. BANDS. Stone rows use days since the oldest stone last moved: 2y+ >=730, 1-2y >=365 and <730, 6-12m >=182.5 and <365, <6m <182.5. Coin columns use weighted_avg_age_days: >1y >=365, 6-12m >=182.5 and <365, 3-6m >=91.25 and <182.5, <3m <91.25. Year = 365 days. Note the collection ceiling: the longest possible dormancy is 885.14 days (first Runestone block 834,708, 2024-03-14), so "2y+" spans 730-885 d and effectively means "never moved since the airdrop". Median wallet dormancy is 882.35 d, p25 is 835.34 d. MATRIX. 16 cells; all 29,198 addresses and all 49,658 stones are placed and no cell is empty. The dominant cell is 2y+ stones x >1y coins with 25,548 addresses (87.4991%) and 37,010 stones. Taking both slow stone rows against the >1y coin column, 27,398 addresses (93.8352%) are old on BOTH clocks. The strict diagonal (2y+/>1y, 1-2y/6-12m, 6-12m/3-6m, <6m/<3m) holds 25,882 addresses (88.6431%). The counter-diagonal is real but small: 81 addresses sit on 2y+ stones while their DOG averages under 3 months, and 85 addresses moved a stone within the last 6 months while their DOG has not moved in over a year. CORRELATION. Pearson r = 0.599700 over n = 29,198 wallets present in both sets, with x = dormancy in days of the wallet's oldest stone and y = weighted_avg_age_days of its DOG. Two robustness variants are included and belong to the same finding: using the wallet's mean stone dormancy instead of its oldest stone gives r = 0.630204, and Spearman rho = 0.461017. The gap between Pearson and Spearman is the ceiling effect above - both variables pile up near their maxima, so ranks inside that pile are noisy while the linear relation stays strong.
